objectives.description: Find maximum or minimum values of quadratic functions by completing the square.
Determine conditions for a quadratic function to be always positive or always negative.
Use quadratic functions as models.
Use discriminant conditions for two real roots, equal roots, or no real roots, including line-curve intersections and tangency.
Solve simultaneous equations in two variables by substitution when one equation is linear.
Solve quadratic inequalities and represent solutions on a number line.
Perform four operations on surds, including rationalising denominators.
Solve equations involving surds.
Multiply and divide polynomials.
Use remainder and factor theorems to factorise polynomials and solve cubic equations.
Use sum and difference of cubes identities.
Resolve partial fractions with distinct or repeated linear factors and a linear factor with x squared plus a positive constant.
Use the Binomial Theorem for a positive integer exponent.
Use factorial and binomial coefficient notation.
Use the general term in a binomial expansion for a positive integer exponent.
Use exponential and logarithmic functions and graphs, logarithm laws, inverse equivalence, and change of base.
Simplify expressions and solve simple exponential and logarithmic equations.
Use exponential and logarithmic functions as models.
Use six trigonometric functions for angles of any magnitude in degrees or radians.
Use principal values of inverse sine, cosine, and tangent.
Use exact trigonometric values for 30, 45, and 60 degrees and corresponding radian angles.
Use amplitude, periodicity, symmetry, and graphs of transformed sine, cosine, and tangent functions.
Use reciprocal, quotient, Pythagorean, compound-angle, and double-angle identities and the R-formula.
Simplify trigonometric expressions.
Solve simple trigonometric equations in a given interval, excluding general solutions.
Prove simple trigonometric identities.
Use trigonometric functions as models.
Determine when two lines are parallel or perpendicular.
Find the midpoint of a line segment.
Find the area of a rectilinear figure.
Use centre-radius and general equations of a circle, excluding problems involving two circles.
Transform power and exponential relationships to linear form and determine constants from a straight-line graph.
Use properties of parallel lines, perpendicular and angle bisectors, triangles, special quadrilaterals, and circles in proofs.
Use congruent and similar triangles in proofs.
Use the midpoint theorem in proofs.
Use the tangent-chord theorem in proofs.
Interpret the derivative as tangent gradient and rate of change and use standard derivative notation.
Differentiate rational powers, trigonometric functions, exponentials, logarithms, and their constant multiples, sums, and differences.
Differentiate products and quotients and apply the Chain Rule.
Analyse increasing and decreasing functions and stationary points, including second-derivative classification.
Apply differentiation to gradients, tangents, normals, connected rates, and maxima and minima.
Interpret integration as reverse differentiation.
Integrate rational powers, sine, cosine, secant squared, exponentials, and their constant multiples, sums, and differences.
Integrate permitted powers, trigonometric functions, and exponentials with a linear inner expression.
Interpret and evaluate definite integrals as areas under curves.
Find areas bounded by a curve and lines, including regions below the x-axis but excluding regions between two curves.
Apply differentiation and integration to straight-line displacement, velocity, and acceleration.
